units.Joel 1:1: The word of the Lord that came to Joel, the son of Bathuel.
units.Joel 1:2: Hear these things, elders, and give ear, all who inhabit the land! Have such things happened in your days or in your fathers’ days?
units.Joel 1:3: Tell your children about these things, and let your children tell their children, and their children a further generation.
units.Joel 1:4: What the caterpillar left, the locust devoured; what the locust left, the bruchus locust devoured; what the bruchus locust left, the blight devoured.
units.Joel 1:5: Sober up, you drunkards, from their wine, and weep! Lament, all who drink wine to intoxication, because gladness and joy have been removed from your mouths.
units.Joel 1:6: For a nation has come up against My land, strong and uncountable. Its teeth are a lion’s teeth, and its grinding teeth a young lion’s.
units.Joel 1:7: It laid My vine waste and shattered My fig trees; searching, it searched it out and cast it away; it whitened its branches.
units.Joel 1:8: Lament to Me more than a bride wrapped in sackcloth for her first husband.
units.Joel 1:9: Sacrifice and drink offering have been removed from the Lord’s house. Mourn, priests who minister at the altar,
units.Joel 1:10: because the plains have suffered. Let the earth mourn, because grain has suffered, wine has dried up, and oil has diminished.
units.Joel 1:11: The farmers have dried up. Lament, estates, over wheat and barley, because the harvest from the field has perished.
units.Joel 1:12: The vine has dried up and the fig trees have diminished; pomegranate, palm, apple tree and all the field’s trees have dried up, because human beings have put joy to shame.
units.Joel 1:13: Wrap yourselves and beat your breasts, priests; lament, ministers of the altar! Enter and sleep in sackcloth, ministers of God, because sacrifice and drink offering have been kept away from your God’s house.
units.Joel 1:14: Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service. Gather elders, all who inhabit the land, into your God’s house, and cry earnestly to the Lord,
units.Joel 1:15: “Alas, alas, alas for the day! For the Lord’s day is near, and it will come like suffering from suffering.”
units.Joel 1:16: Before your eyes food was destroyed, and gladness and joy from your God’s house.
units.Joel 1:17: Heifers leaped at their feeding troughs; storehouses disappeared, winepresses were demolished, because grain dried up.
units.Joel 1:18: What shall we store up for ourselves? Herds of cattle wept because they had no pasture, and flocks of sheep disappeared.
units.Joel 1:19: To Thee, Lord, I will cry, because fire consumed the beautiful places of the wilderness, and flame kindled all the field’s trees.
units.Joel 1:20: Even the animals of the plain looked up toward Thee, because outlets of water dried up, and fire devoured the beautiful places of the wilderness.
units.Joel 2:1: Blow a trumpet in Zion! Proclaim on My holy mountain, and let all who inhabit the land be thrown into turmoil, because the Lord’s day is present; it is near,
units.Joel 2:2: a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and mist. Like dawn a numerous and strong people will be poured over the mountains. Its like has never existed, nor will another follow it through the years, for generations upon generations.
units.Joel 2:3: Before it is consuming fire, and behind it a kindled flame. The land before its face is like a garden of delight, and behind it a desolate plain; no one will escape it.
units.Joel 2:4: Their appearance is like the sight of horses; like riders they will pursue.
units.Joel 2:5: With a sound like chariots they will leap upon mountain peaks, like the sound of a fiery flame devouring stubble, like a numerous and strong people arrayed for war.
units.Joel 2:6: Before it peoples will be crushed; every face is like the scorching of a pot.
units.Joel 2:7: Like fighters they will run, and like soldiers they will climb the walls. Each will go on his own road, and they certainly will not turn aside from their paths,
units.Joel 2:8: and no one will hold back from his brother. Burdened with their weapons they will go, and among their missiles they will fall, yet they will certainly not be destroyed.
units.Joel 2:9: They will seize the city and run upon the walls; they will climb upon the houses and enter through windows like thieves.
units.Joel 2:10: Before them the earth will be thrown into turmoil and heaven shaken; the sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will sink their brightness.
units.Joel 2:11: The Lord will give His voice before His force, because His camp is very large, because the works of His words are strong. For the Lord’s day is great, great and very manifest; who will be sufficient for it?
units.Joel 2:12: “And now,” says the Lord your God, “turn to Me with your whole heart, with fasting, weeping and mourning.”
units.Joel 2:13: Tear your hearts, not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God, because He is merciful and compassionate, patient and abundant in mercy, and relents concerning calamities.
units.Joel 2:14: Who knows whether He will turn and relent and leave a blessing behind Him, a sacrifice and drink offering for the Lord our God?
units.Joel 2:15: Blow a trumpet in Zion! Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service.
units.Joel 2:16: Gather the people; consecrate the congregation. Choose elders; gather infants nursing at breasts. Let the bridegroom leave his bedroom and the bride her bridal chamber.
units.Joel 2:17: In the midst of the altar’s platform the priests who minister to the Lord will weep and say, “Spare Thy people, Lord, and do not give Thine inheritance to reproach, for nations to rule over them, so that they do not say among the nations, ‘Where is their God?’”
units.Joel 2:18: Then the Lord became jealous for His land and spared His people.
units.Joel 2:19: The Lord answered His people: “Look, I am sending out to you grain, wine and oil, and you will be filled with them. I will no longer give you over to reproach among the nations,
units.Joel 2:20: and I will drive away from you the one from the north and thrust it into a waterless land. I will make its front disappear into the first sea and its rear into the last sea; its decay will rise, and its stench will rise, because it magnified its deeds.”
units.Joel 2:21: Take courage, land! Rejoice and be glad, because the Lord has done great things.
units.Joel 2:22: Take courage, animals of the plain, because the wilderness plains have sprouted, because a tree bore its fruit; vine and fig tree have given their strength.
units.Joel 2:23: Children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the Lord your God, because He gave you food for righteousness, and He will rain upon you early and late rainfall as before.
units.Joel 2:24: Threshing floors will be filled with grain, and winepresses will overflow with wine and oil.
units.Joel 2:25: “I will repay you for the years the locust devoured, the bruchus locust, the blight and the caterpillar—My great force that I sent among you.
units.Joel 2:26: You will eat abundantly and be filled, and praise the name of the Lord your God for the wonders He has done with you. My people will certainly never be put to shame,
units.Joel 2:27: and you will recognize that I am in Israel’s midst, that I am the Lord your God and there is no other besides Me. All My people will certainly never again be put to shame.”
units.Joel 3:1: “And it shall be after these things, that I will pour out of My Spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your elders shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions.
units.Joel 3:2: Even upon male slaves and female slaves in those days I will pour out of My Spirit.
units.Joel 3:3: I will give wonders in heaven and upon the earth: blood, fire and a vapor of smoke.
units.Joel 3:4: The sun will turn to darkness and the moon to blood before the coming of the Lord’s great and manifest day.
units.Joel 3:5: Everyone who calls upon the Lord’s name will be saved, for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be one who escapes, as the Lord said, and bearers of good news whom the Lord has called.”
units.Joel 4:1: “For look, in those days and at that time, when I turn back the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,
units.Joel 4:2: I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment with them over My people and My inheritance Israel, who were scattered among the nations; and they divided up My land
units.Joel 4:3: and cast lots over My people; they gave the boys to prostitutes and sold the girls for wine, which they drank.
units.Joel 4:4: What have you to do with Me, Tyre and Sidon and all Galilee of foreigners? Are you repaying Me a recompense? Or do you bear a sharp grudge against Me? I will speedily repay your recompense upon your heads,
units.Joel 4:5: because you took My silver and gold and brought My chosen and beautiful things into your temples,
units.Joel 4:6: and sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem to the sons of the Greeks, so as to thrust them out of their own borders.
units.Joel 4:7: Look, I am rousing them from the place to which you sold them, and I will repay your recompense upon your heads,
units.Joel 4:8: and I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the sons of Judah, and they will sell them into captivity to a nation far away, because the Lord has spoken.”
units.Joel 4:9: Proclaim these things among the nations: Consecrate war! Rouse the fighters! Draw near and come up, all soldiers!
units.Joel 4:10: Beat your plows into swords and your sickles into lances; let the powerless say, “I am strong!”
units.Joel 4:11: Assemble and enter, all surrounding nations, and gather there! Let the meek become a fighter!
units.Joel 4:12: Let all the nations be roused and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, because there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
units.Joel 4:13: Send out sickles, because the vintage is at hand! Enter and tread, because the winepress is full; the vats overflow, because their evils have multiplied.
units.Joel 4:14: Sounds rang out in the Valley of Judgment, because the Lord’s day is near in the Valley of Judgment.
units.Joel 4:15: The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will sink their brightness.
units.Joel 4:16: The Lord will cry out from Zion and give His voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth will shake. But the Lord will spare His people, and the Lord will strengthen the sons of Israel.
units.Joel 4:17: You will recognize that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Zion on My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be a holy city, and foreigners will no longer pass through her.
units.Joel 4:18: On that day mountains will drip sweetness, hills will flow with milk, and all Judah’s water outlets will flow with water. A spring will come out of the Lord’s house and water the Wadi of Rushes.
units.Joel 4:19: Egypt will become desolate, and Idumea a desolate plain, because of injustices concerning the sons of Judah, because they poured out righteous blood in their land.
units.Joel 4:20: But Judea will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem for generations upon generations.
units.Joel 4:21: “I will avenge their blood, and I will certainly not acquit.” And the Lord will dwell in Zion.
units.Exodus 10:1: The Lord said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and his attendants’ hearts, so that these signs may come upon them in succession,
units.Exodus 10:2: that you may tell in the ears of your children, and of your children’s children, how I have mocked the Egyptians, and My signs which I have performed among them; and you shall know that I am the Lord.”
units.Exodus 10:3: And Moses and Aaron went in before Pharaoh, and said to him, “Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: How long will you refuse to reverence Me? Let My people go, that they may serve Me.
units.Exodus 10:4: But if you will not let My people go, behold, at this hour tomorrow I will bring many locusts upon all your borders.
units.Exodus 10:5: And they shall cover the face of the land, and you shall not be able to see the land; and they shall devour all that remains of the land which the hail left to you, and every tree growing for you upon the land.
units.Exodus 10:6: And your houses shall be filled, and the houses of your attendants, and all the houses throughout the land of the Egyptians, as neither your fathers nor their forefathers have ever seen, from the day they came upon the earth to this day.” And Moses turned and went out from Pharaoh.
units.Exodus 10:7: And Pharaoh’s attendants said to him, “How long shall this be a hindrance to us? Let the men go, that they may serve their God. Or do you want to know that Egypt is destroyed?”
units.Exodus 10:8: Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. He said to them, “Go, serve your God. But who are those who will go?”
units.Exodus 10:9: Moses said, “We will go with our young men and our elders, with our sons and our daughters, and with our sheep and our cattle, for it is a feast of the Lord our God.”
units.Exodus 10:10: And he said to them, “So be it, the Lord be with you! When I let you go, shall I also let your households go? Behold, evil lies before you.
units.Exodus 10:11: Not so; let the men go, and serve God, for this is what you seek.” And they drove them out from Pharaoh’s presence.
units.Exodus 10:12: And the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt, and let locusts come up upon the land; and they shall devour every plant of the land, and all the fruit of the trees which the hail has left.”
units.Exodus 10:13: Moses raised his staff toward heaven, and the Lord brought a south wind upon the land all that day and all that night. When morning came, the south wind carried up the locusts.
units.Exodus 10:14: It brought them up over all the land of Egypt, and they settled throughout Egypt’s territory in immense numbers. There had never been such locusts before, nor would there be afterward.
units.Exodus 10:15: They covered the surface of the land, and the land was ruined. They devoured all the vegetation of the land and all the fruit of the trees that the hail had left. Nothing green remained on the trees or among the vegetation of the field throughout the land of Egypt.
units.Exodus 10:16: Pharaoh hurried to call Moses and Aaron and said, “I have sinned before the Lord your God and against you.
units.Exodus 10:17: Forgive my sin this once more, and pray to the Lord your God to remove this death from me.”
units.Exodus 10:18: Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to God.
units.Exodus 10:19: The Lord turned a very strong wind from the sea. It lifted the locusts and cast them into the Red Sea. Not one locust remained in all Egypt’s territory.
units.Exodus 10:20: The Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not let the sons of Israel go.
units.Jeremiah 4:5: Announce in Judah, and let it be heard in Jerusalem; say: Signal with a trumpet over the land, and cry loudly! Say: Gather, and let us enter the walled cities!
units.Jeremiah 4:6: Take up and flee to Zion; hurry, do not stand still, for I am bringing evils from the north and great crushing.
units.Jeremiah 4:7: A lion has gone up from his enclosure; destroying nations, he has set out and left his place to make the land a desolation, and cities will be demolished so that they are not inhabited.
units.Jeremiah 4:8: For these things, gird yourselves with sackcloth, beat yourselves in mourning and wail, because the Lord’s fury has not turned away from you.
units.Jeremiah 4:9: And it will be on that day, says the Lord: the king’s heart and the rulers’ heart will perish, and the priests will be beside themselves and the prophets astonished.
units.Jeremiah 5:15: Behold, I am bringing a nation upon you from far away, house of Israel, says the Lord, a nation whose language’s sound you will not understand.
units.Jeremiah 5:17: and they will devour your harvest and your bread, and devour your sons and daughters, and devour your sheep and calves, and devour your vineyards and fig orchards and olive groves; and with a sword they will thresh your fortified cities, in which you have trusted.
units.Jeremiah 6:22: Thus says the Lord: Behold, a people comes from the north, and nations will be roused from the earth’s extremity.
units.Jeremiah 6:23: They will grasp bow and spear; it is ruthless and will show no mercy. Its voice is like a surging sea; on horses and chariots it will draw up like fire for war against you, daughter of Zion.
units.Jeremiah 6:24: We heard the report of them; our hands were paralyzed. Affliction seized us, labor pains like a woman giving birth.
units.Jeremiah 6:25: Do not go out into a field or walk on the roads, because the enemies’ sword dwells all around.
units.Jeremiah 6:26: Daughter of My people, gird yourself with sackcloth; sprinkle yourself with ashes. Make mourning for yourself for a beloved one, a pitiful lament, because misery will suddenly come upon you.
units.Jeremiah 6:27: I have made you a tester among tested peoples, and you will know Me when I test their way.
units.Jeremiah 14:1: And the Lord’s word came to Jeremiah concerning the lack of rain:
units.Jeremiah 14:2: Judea mourned, and her gates were emptied and darkened upon the earth, and Jerusalem’s cry rose.
units.Jeremiah 14:3: Her magnates sent their younger ones for water; they came to wells and found no water and brought back their vessels empty.
units.Jeremiah 14:4: And the land’s works failed because there was no rain; the farmers were ashamed and covered their heads.
units.Jeremiah 14:5: And deer in the field gave birth and abandoned their young, because there was no pasture.
units.Jeremiah 14:6: Wild donkeys stood in wooded valleys; they drew in wind, their eyes failed, because there was no grass, because of a people of injustice.
units.Jeremiah 14:7: If our sins stood against us, Lord, act for us for Thine own sake, because our sins before Thee are many, because we sinned against Thee.
units.Isaiah 24:1: Behold, the Lord is destroying the inhabited world; He will make it desolate, uncover its face and scatter those dwelling in it.
units.Isaiah 24:2: The people will be like the priest, the slave like the master, the maidservant like the mistress; the buyer will be like the seller, the lender like the borrower, and the debtor like the one to whom he owes a debt.
units.Isaiah 24:3: The earth will be utterly destroyed, and the earth utterly plundered, for the Lord’s mouth has spoken these things.
units.Isaiah 24:4: The earth mourned, the inhabited world was destroyed, and the earth’s high ones mourned.
units.Isaiah 24:5: The earth acted lawlessly because of those dwelling in it, because they transgressed the law and changed the ordinances, an everlasting covenant.
units.Isaiah 24:6: Therefore a curse will consume the earth, because those dwelling in it sinned. Therefore those dwelling on the earth will be poor, and few people will be left.
units.Isaiah 24:7: Wine will mourn, the vine will mourn, and all who gladden the soul will groan.
units.Isaiah 24:8: The joy of tambourines has ceased; the impudence and wealth of the ungodly have ceased; the lyre’s sound has ceased.
units.Isaiah 24:9: They were ashamed and did not drink wine; sikera became bitter to those drinking it.
units.Isaiah 24:10: Every city was deserted; he will shut a house so that none may enter.
units.Isaiah 24:11: Wail over wine everywhere! All the earth’s gladness has ceased.
units.Isaiah 24:12: Cities will be left deserted, and abandoned houses will perish.
units.Isaiah 24:13: All these things will happen on the earth, among the nations: as when someone gleans an olive tree, so they will glean them, even when the grape harvest has ceased.
units.Hosea 9:1: Do not rejoice, Israel, or be glad like the peoples, because you prostituted yourself away from your God; you loved gifts on every threshing floor of grain.
units.Hosea 9:2: Threshing floor and winepress did not know them, and wine deceived them.
units.Hosea 9:3: They did not dwell in the Lord’s land; Ephraim dwelt in Egypt, and among the Assyrians they will eat unclean things.
units.Hosea 9:4: They did not pour wine to the Lord or make it pleasant to Him. Their sacrifices are like bread of mourning to them; all who eat them will be defiled, because their loaves for their own lives will not enter the Lord’s house.
units.Haggai 1:5: And now, thus says the Lord Almighty: Set your hearts upon your ways.
units.Haggai 1:6: You sowed much and brought in little; you ate, but were not satisfied; you drank, but not to intoxication; you clothed yourselves, but were not warmed in them. The one gathering wages gathered them into a bundle with holes.
units.Haggai 1:7: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Place your hearts upon your ways.
units.Haggai 1:8: Go up onto the mountain, cut wood and rebuild the house. I will take pleasure in it and be glorified, said the Lord.
units.Haggai 1:9: You looked for much, and it came to little; it was brought into the house, and I blew it away. Therefore, thus says the Lord Almighty: Because My house is desolate, while each of you hurries to his own house,
units.Haggai 1:10: therefore heaven will hold back dew, and the earth will withhold its produce.
units.Haggai 1:11: I will bring a sword upon the land and the mountains, upon grain, wine and oil, and whatever the earth produces, upon people and livestock, and upon all the labors of their hands.”
units.Deuteronomy 12:5: but unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose in one of your tribes, to set His name there, that it may be called upon, you shall seek and come thither.
units.Deuteronomy 12:6: And you shall bring thither your whole burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, and your firstfruits, and your vowed offerings, and your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your cattle and of your sheep.
units.Deuteronomy 12:7: And you shall eat there before the Lord your God, and rejoice in all that you put your hand unto, you and your houses, because the Lord your God has blessed you.
units.Psalms 103:10: He sends springs into the ravines; waters will pass between the mountains.
units.Psalms 103:11: They give drink to all the beasts of the field; wild donkeys will receive it for their thirst.
units.Psalms 103:12: Upon them the birds of heaven will nest; from among the rocks they will give voice.
units.Psalms 103:13: He waters mountains from His upper chambers; the earth will be filled with the fruit of Thy works.
units.Psalms 103:14: He makes grass spring up for livestock and green plants for the service of humans, to bring bread out of the earth;
units.Psalms 103:15: and wine gladdens the human heart, to brighten the face with oil, and bread makes the human heart firm.
units.Isaiah 13:1: The vision that Isaiah son of Amos saw against Babylon.
units.Isaiah 13:2: Raise a signal on a level mountain, lift your voice to them, do not fear, beckon with the hand: “Open, rulers!”
units.Isaiah 13:3: I command, and I lead them; they are consecrated, and I lead them. Giants are coming to fulfill My wrath, rejoicing and acting insolently together.
units.Isaiah 13:4: A sound of many nations upon the mountains, like many nations; a sound of kings and gathered nations. The Lord Sabaoth has commanded an armed nation,
units.Isaiah 13:5: to come from a distant land, from the farthest edge of heaven’s foundation—the Lord and His armed fighters—to destroy the whole inhabited world.
units.Isaiah 13:6: Wail, for the Lord’s day is near, and shattering will come from God.
units.Isaiah 13:7: Therefore every hand will slacken, and every human soul grow cowardly;
units.Isaiah 13:8: the envoys will be troubled, and labor pains will hold them like those of a woman giving birth. They will lament to one another and be distraught, and change their face as to flame.
units.Isaiah 13:9: For behold, the Lord’s incurable day comes, of wrath and anger, to make the whole inhabited world deserted and destroy its sinners from it.
units.Isaiah 13:10: For heaven’s stars, Orion and all heaven’s array will not give light; it will grow dark as the sun rises, and the moon will not give its light.
units.Isaiah 13:11: I will ordain evils for the whole inhabited world, and for the ungodly their sins; I will destroy the insolence of the lawless and lower the insolence of the proud.
units.Isaiah 13:12: Those left will be more precious than unrefined gold, and a human being more precious than the stone from Souphir.
units.Isaiah 13:13: For heaven will be enraged, and the earth shaken from its foundations through the fury of the Lord Sabaoth’s anger, on the day when His wrath comes upon it.
units.Psalms 103:1: Of David. Bless the Lord, my soul. Lord my God, Thou hast become very great; Thou hast clothed Thyself in praise and dignity,
units.Psalms 103:2: wrapping Thyself in light like a garment, stretching out heaven like a hide curtain;
units.Psalms 103:3: He roofs His upper chambers in waters, makes clouds His means of ascent, and walks on the wings of winds.
units.Psalms 103:4: He makes His angels winds, and His ministers a burning fire.
units.Psalms 103:5: He founded the earth on its stability; it will not be tilted for an age of ages.
units.Psalms 103:6: The deep is His covering like a garment; waters will stand upon the mountains.
units.Psalms 103:7: At Thy rebuke they will flee; at the voice of Thy thunder they will become afraid.
units.Psalms 103:8: Mountains rise and plains descend to the place Thou didst found for them.
units.Psalms 103:9: Thou didst set a boundary they will not pass, nor will they return to cover the earth.
units.Nahum 2:1: Look, upon the mountains are the feet of one bringing good news and announcing peace! Celebrate your feasts, Judah; repay your vows. For they will no longer pass through you into decay. It has been completed; it has been removed.
units.Nahum 2:2: One who breathes into your face has come up, rescuing from affliction. Watch the road; hold your waist firm; act courageously with great strength,
units.Nahum 2:3: because the Lord turned away Jacob’s arrogance, as Israel’s arrogance; for those shaking them out shook out both them and their vine branches; they ruined
units.Nahum 2:4: the weapons of their might from among people, mighty men playing in fire. The reins of their chariots are on the day of his preparation, and the horsemen will be thrown into uproar
units.Nahum 2:5: in the roads, and the chariots will be thrown into confusion and entangled in the squares; their appearance is like torches of fire and lightning flashing past.
units.Nahum 2:6: Their nobles will remember and flee by day; they will weaken on their journey, hurry to the walls and prepare their defenses.
units.Nahum 2:7: The river gates were opened, and the royal palace collapsed.
units.Nahum 2:8: The foundation was uncovered, and she was going up, and her slave women were being led away like doves murmuring in their hearts.
units.Nahum 2:9: Nineveh—her waters are like a swimming pool; they were fleeing and did not stop, and there was no one looking back.
units.Nahum 2:10: They were plundering silver; they were plundering gold. There was no limit to her adornment; they have been weighed down beyond all her desirable vessels.
units.Nahum 2:11: Shaking out, tossing up and boiling over; broken hearts, loosening knees, pangs at every waist, and every face like the scorching of a pot.
units.Nahum 2:12: Where is the lions’ dwelling and the pasture that belonged to the cubs, where a lion went to enter there, a lion’s cub, and no one frightened them?
units.Nahum 2:13: A lion seized enough for his cubs and strangled for his lions; he filled his nest with prey and his dwelling with plunder.
units.Nahum 2:14: Look, I am against you, says the Lord Almighty. I will burn your multitude in smoke; the sword will consume your lions. I will destroy your prey from the earth, and your deeds will never again be heard.
units.Nahum 3:1: O city of bloodshed, wholly false, full of injustice! Prey will not be touched.
units.Nahum 3:2: The sound of whips and the sound of shaking wheels, of a pursuing horse and a jolting chariot,
units.Nahum 3:3: and of a mounting horseman, a flashing sword and glittering weapons, a multitude of slain and a grievous fall! There was no limit to her nations, and they will weaken in their bodies
units.Nahum 3:4: because of the multitude of prostitution. A prostitute, beautiful and pleasing, mistress of potions, selling nations through her prostitution and tribes through her potions,
units.Nahum 3:5: look, I am against you, says the Lord God Almighty. I will expose your hind parts over your face and show nations your shame and kingdoms your dishonor,
units.Nahum 3:6: and cast abomination upon you according to your impurities, and make you an example,
units.Nahum 3:7: and everyone seeing you will spring away and say, “Miserable Nineveh! Who will lament her? Where shall I seek consolation for her?”
units.Nahum 3:8: Prepare a portion; tune a string; prepare a portion, Amon, who dwells among rivers, water around her, whose dominion was the sea and whose walls were water,
units.Nahum 3:9: and Ethiopia was her strength, and Egypt, and there is no limit to the flight; Libyans became her helpers.
units.Nahum 3:10: She too will go into deportation as a captive; they will dash her infants to the ground at the head of all her roads, cast lots for all her glorious things; and all her nobles will be bound in handcuffs.
units.Proverbs 30:24: Four things are smallest upon the earth, yet these are wiser than the wise:
units.Proverbs 30:25: the ants, which have no strength, yet prepare their food in summer;
units.Proverbs 30:26: and the rock badgers, a nation without strength, which made their own houses in rocks;
units.Proverbs 30:27: the locust is without a king, yet marches out in good order at one command;
units.Proverbs 30:28: And the lizard, bracing itself with its hands and being easily caught, lives in a king’s fortifications.
units.Jeremiah 9:17: and let them take up a dirge over you; let your eyes bring down tears, and let your eyelids flow with water.
units.Jeremiah 9:18: For a voice of lament was heard in Zion: How we suffered misery and were greatly ashamed, because we abandoned the land and threw away our dwellings!
units.Jeremiah 9:19: Hear God’s word now, women, and let your ears receive His mouth’s words; teach your daughters lament, and each woman her neighbor a dirge.
units.Jeremiah 9:20: For death climbed through your windows and entered your land, to wipe out little children outside and young men from the squares.
units.Jeremiah 9:21: And people’s dead will become an example on the surface of your land’s plain, and like grass behind one reaping, and there will be no one gathering.
units.Matthew 24:1: Jesus went out from the temple and was going away, when His disciples came to show Him the temple buildings.
units.Matthew 24:2: He answered them, “Do you not see all these things? Truly I tell you, not one stone will be left here upon another that will not be thrown down.”
units.Matthew 24:3: As He sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately, saying, “Tell us, when will these things happen, and what is the sign of Thy coming and the consummation of the age?”
units.Matthew 24:29: Immediately after the affliction of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its brightness, the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
units.Matthew 24:30: Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn; they will see the Son of Man coming upon the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
units.Matthew 24:31: He will send His angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather His chosen from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
units.Malachi 3:1: “Look, I am sending out My messenger, and he will look to a way before My face. Suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to His own sanctuary, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Look, he is coming,” says the Lord Almighty.
units.Malachi 3:2: And who will endure the day of his entrance? Or who will stand at his appearance? For he enters like a smelting fire and like launderers’ herb.
units.Malachi 3:3: He will sit, smelting and purifying as with silver and gold. He will cleanse the sons of Levi and melt them like gold and silver, and they will be those who bring a sacrifice to the Lord in righteousness.
units.Malachi 3:4: And the sacrifice of Judah and Jerusalem will please the Lord, as in the days of old and as in the former years.
units.Deuteronomy 30:1: And it shall be, when all these things come upon you, the blessing and the curse which I have set before your face, and you receive them into your heart among all the nations whither the Lord has scattered you,
units.Deuteronomy 30:2: and you return unto the Lord your God, and obey His voice according to all that I command you this day, with all your heart and with all your soul,
units.Deuteronomy 30:3: then the Lord shall heal your sins, and have mercy upon you, and shall gather you again from all the nations whither the Lord has scattered you.
units.Exodus 34:1: The Lord said to Moses, “Hew for yourself two tablets of stone like the first, and come up to Me on the mountain. I will write upon the tablets the words that were upon the first tablets, which you shattered.
units.Exodus 34:2: Be ready in the morning, come up to Mount Sinai, and stand before Me there on the mountain’s summit.
units.Exodus 34:3: Let no one come up with you or be seen anywhere on the mountain. Neither sheep nor cattle shall graze near that mountain.”
units.Exodus 34:4: Moses cut two stone tablets like the first. He rose early and went up Mount Sinai as the Lord commanded him, taking the two stone tablets.
units.Exodus 34:5: The Lord descended in a cloud, stood beside him there, and called upon the name of the Lord.
units.Exodus 34:6: The Lord passed before him and proclaimed, “The Lord God, compassionate and merciful, slow to anger, abundant in mercy and true,
units.Exodus 34:7: preserving righteousness and showing mercy to thousands, taking away lawlessness, injustice, and sins, yet not cleansing the guilty, bringing the fathers’ lawlessness upon children and children’s children to the third and fourth generation.”
units.Exodus 34:8: Moses quickly bowed to the ground and worshipped.
units.Exodus 34:9: He said, “If I have found grace before Thee, let my Lord go with us, for this is a stiff-necked people. Thou shalt take away our sins and our lawlessness, and we shall be Thine.”
units.Jonah 3:5: The people of Nineveh believed God, proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from their greatest to their least.
units.Jonah 3:6: The word reached the king of Nineveh. He rose from his throne, took his robe off himself, wrapped himself in sackcloth and sat in ashes.
units.Jonah 3:7: It was proclaimed and declared in Nineveh from the king and his nobles: “Let people and livestock, cattle and sheep, taste nothing; let them not graze or drink water.”
units.Jonah 3:8: People and livestock clothed themselves in sackcloth, and they cried earnestly to God. Each turned away from his evil way and from the injustice in their hands, saying:
units.Jonah 3:9: “Who knows whether God will relent and turn from His fierce anger, so that we certainly do not perish?”
units.Jonah 3:10: God saw their deeds, that they had turned from their evil ways. God relented concerning the calamity He had said He would bring upon them, and He did not do it.
units.Jonah 4:1: Jonah was grieved with great grief and was disturbed.
units.Jonah 4:2: He prayed to the Lord and said, “O Lord, were these not my words while I was still in my own land? That is why I was quick to flee to Tarshish, for I knew that Thou art merciful and compassionate, patient, abundant in mercy, and relenting concerning calamities.
units.Jonah 4:3: And now, Master Lord, take my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live.”
units.Jonah 4:4: The Lord said to Jonah, “Are you deeply grieved?”
units.Zechariah 8:1: The word of the Lord Almighty came, saying:
units.Zechariah 8:2: “Thus says the Lord Almighty: I have been jealous for Jerusalem and Zion with great jealousy; with great wrath I have been jealous for her.
units.Zechariah 8:3: Thus says the Lord: I will return to Zion and dwell within Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the True City, and the mountain of the Lord Almighty a Holy Mountain.
units.Zechariah 8:4: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Old men and old women will again sit in Jerusalem’s squares, each holding a staff in hand because of many days.
units.Zechariah 8:5: The city’s squares will be filled with boys and girls playing in her squares.
units.Zechariah 8:6: Thus says the Lord Almighty: If it is impossible before this people’s remnant in those days, surely it will not also be impossible before Me? says the Lord Almighty.
units.Zechariah 8:7: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Look, I am rescuing My people from the eastern land and from the western land,
units.Zechariah 8:8: and I will bring them in and dwell within Jerusalem. They will be My people, and I will be their God in truth and righteousness.
units.Zephaniah 1:14: For the Lord’s great day is near, near and very swift. The sound of the Lord’s day is bitter and harsh; it is appointed mighty.
units.Zephaniah 1:15: That day is a day of wrath, a day of affliction and constraint, a day of untimely ruin and destruction, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and mist,
units.Zephaniah 1:16: a day of trumpet and shouting against fortified cities and high corners.
units.Zephaniah 1:17: I will press people hard, and they will walk like the blind because they sinned against the Lord. He will pour out their blood like dust and their flesh like dung.
units.Zephaniah 1:18: Their silver and gold will certainly not rescue them on the day of the Lord’s wrath. In the fire of His jealousy all the earth will be consumed, for He will bring completion and haste upon all the earth’s inhabitants.
units.Ezekiel 36:33: Thus says the Lord: On the day I cleanse you from all your lawless deeds, I will cause the cities to be inhabited, and the wilderness places will be rebuilt.
units.Ezekiel 36:34: The devastated land will be worked, instead of lying devastated before every passerby’s eyes.
units.Ezekiel 36:35: They will say, “That devastated land has become like a garden of delight, and the deserted, devastated, razed cities stand fortified.”
units.Ezekiel 36:36: The nations remaining around you will know that I, the Lord, have rebuilt the razed places and planted the devastated places. I, the Lord, have spoken and will act.
units.Deuteronomy 31:9: And Moses wrote the words of this law in a book, and gave it unto the priests, the sons of Levi, who bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and unto the elders of the sons of Israel.
units.Deuteronomy 31:10: And Moses commanded them in that day, saying, After seven years, at the appointed time of the year of release, at the Feast of the Pitching of Tents,
units.Deuteronomy 31:11: when all Israel comes together to appear before the Lord your God in the place which the Lord shall choose, you shall read this law before all Israel in their hearing.
units.Deuteronomy 31:12: Gather the people, the men, and the women, and the children, and the sojourner who is in your cities, that they may hear, and that they may learn to fear the Lord your God; and they shall hearken to do all the words of this law.
units.Deuteronomy 31:13: And their sons, who do not know, shall hear and learn to fear the Lord your God all the days that they live upon the land into which you are crossing the Jordan to inherit it.
units.Psalms 78:1: A psalm for Asaph. God, nations entered Thine inheritance; they defiled Thy holy temple; they made Jerusalem into a fruit-watchman’s hut.
units.Psalms 78:2: They made the dead bodies of Thy servants food for the birds of heaven, the flesh of Thy holy ones for the beasts of the earth.
units.Psalms 78:3: They poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.
units.Psalms 78:4: We became a reproach to our neighbors, sneering and ridicule to those around us.
units.Psalms 78:5: How long, Lord? Wilt Thou be angry to the end? Will Thy jealousy blaze like fire?
units.Psalms 78:6: Pour out Thy wrath upon nations that do not know Thee, and upon kingdoms that did not call on Thy name,
units.Psalms 78:7: for they devoured Jacob and made his place desolate.
units.Psalms 78:8: Do not remember our ancient acts of lawlessness; let Thy compassions swiftly reach us first, for we became very poor.
units.Psalms 78:9: Help us, God our Savior. For the glory of Thy name, Lord, rescue us, and be propitious toward our sins for Thy name’s sake,
units.Psalms 78:10: lest the nations say, “Where is their God?” And let vengeance for the poured-out blood of Thy servants be known among the nations before our eyes.
units.Psalms 78:11: Let the groaning of those in bonds enter before Thee; according to the greatness of Thine arm, preserve the sons of those put to death.
units.Psalms 78:12: Repay our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom their insult with which they insulted Thee, Lord.
units.Psalms 78:13: But we, Thy people and the sheep of Thy pasture, will give Thee thanks for ever; from generation to generation we will proclaim Thy praise.
units.Deuteronomy 11:8: And you shall keep all His commandments which I command you this day, that you may live and multiply, and enter and inherit the land whither you pass over the Jordan to inherit it,
units.Deuteronomy 11:9: that you may prolong your days upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give unto them and unto their seed after them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
units.Deuteronomy 11:10: For the land whither you go to inherit it is not as the land of Egypt, whence you came forth, where they sow seed and water it with their feet, as a garden of herbs.
units.Deuteronomy 11:11: But the land whither you go to inherit it is a land of hills and plains; it shall drink water of the rain of heaven,
units.Deuteronomy 11:12: a land which the Lord your God cares for; the eyes of the Lord your God are always upon it, from the beginning of the year even unto the end of the year.
units.Deuteronomy 11:13: And if you diligently hearken unto all His commandments which I command you this day, to love the Lord your God, and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul,
units.Deuteronomy 11:14: He shall give the rain unto your land in its season, the early and the latter rain; and you shall gather in your grain, and your wine, and your oil.
units.Deuteronomy 11:15: And He shall give grass in your fields for your cattle; and when you have eaten and are filled,
units.Deuteronomy 11:16: take heed unto yourself, lest your heart be enlarged, and you transgress, and serve other gods, and bow down unto them,
units.Deuteronomy 11:17: and the Lord be kindled to wrath against you, and shut up heaven, so that there is no rain, and the land does not yield her fruit, and you perish speedily from the good land which the Lord has given you.
units.Isaiah 34:1: Draw near, nations, and hear, rulers! Let the earth and those in it hear, the inhabited world and the people in it!
units.Isaiah 34:2: For the Lord’s wrath is against all nations, and anger against their number, to destroy them and hand them over to slaughter.
units.Isaiah 34:3: Their wounded and dead will be thrown out; their odor will rise, and mountains will be soaked with their blood.
units.Isaiah 34:4: Heaven will roll up like a scroll, and all the stars will fall like leaves from a vine, like leaves falling from a fig tree.
units.Psalms 125:1: A song of the ascents. When the Lord turned back Zion’s captivity, we became like those comforted.
units.Psalms 125:2: Then our mouth was filled with joy and our tongue with exultation. Then they will say among the nations, “The Lord has done great things with them.”
units.Psalms 125:3: The Lord has done great things with us; we became glad.
units.Psalms 125:4: Turn back our captivity, Lord, like torrents in the south.
units.Psalms 125:5: Those sowing in tears will reap with exultation.
units.Psalms 125:6: Going, they went and wept, carrying their seeds; but coming, they will arrive with exultation, carrying their sheaves.
units.Proverbs 3:5: Trust God with your whole heart; do not exalt yourself in your own wisdom.
units.Proverbs 3:6: In all your ways acknowledge her, that she may cut your ways straight; and your foot will surely not stumble.
units.Proverbs 3:7: Do not be prudent in your own estimation; fear God and turn away from every evil.
units.Proverbs 3:8: Then there will be healing for your body and care for your bones.
units.Proverbs 3:9: Honor the Lord from your righteous labors, and offer Him firstfruits from your fruits of righteousness,
units.Proverbs 3:10: so that your storerooms may be filled with an abundance of grain and your vats gush with wine.
units.Deuteronomy 8:1: All the commandments which I command you this day you shall take heed to do, that you may live and multiply, and enter and inherit the land which the Lord your God sware unto your fathers.
units.Deuteronomy 8:2: And you shall remember all the way wherein the Lord your God led you in the wilderness, to afflict you and to test you, that the things in your heart might be known, whether you would keep His commandments or not.
units.Deuteronomy 8:3: And He afflicted you, and made you hunger, and fed you with manna, which your fathers did not know, that He might declare unto you that man shall not live by bread alone, but man shall live by every word that proceeds through the mouth of God.
units.Deuteronomy 8:4: Your garments did not wear out upon you, neither did your feet become calloused; behold, these forty years.
units.Deuteronomy 8:5: And you shall know in your heart that, as a man chastens his son, so shall the Lord your God chasten you.
units.Deuteronomy 8:6: And you shall keep the commandments of the Lord your God, to walk in His ways and to fear Him.
units.Deuteronomy 8:7: For the Lord your God brings you into a good and spacious land, where are torrents of water and springs of the depths, flowing through the plains and through the hills;
units.Deuteronomy 8:8: a land of wheat and barley, vines, fig trees, and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey,
units.Deuteronomy 8:9: a land wherein you shall eat your bread without poverty, and shall lack nothing; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills you shall mine copper.
units.Deuteronomy 8:10: And you shall eat and be filled, and bless the Lord your God upon the good land which He has given you.
units.Deuteronomy 4:32: Ask now of the former days that were before you, from the day when God created man upon the earth, and from one end of heaven unto the other: has there been anything like this great matter, or has such a thing been heard?
units.Deuteronomy 4:33: Has a nation heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and lived?
units.Deuteronomy 4:34: Or has God attempted to go and take unto Himself a nation from the midst of a nation, by trial, and by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand, and by an uplifted arm, and by great visions, according to all that the Lord our God did in Egypt before your eyes?
units.Deuteronomy 4:35: That you might know that the Lord your God, He is God, and there is none beside Him.
units.Deuteronomy 4:36: Out of heaven His voice was made heard, to instruct you; and upon earth He showed you His great fire, and you heard His words out of the midst of the fire.
units.Deuteronomy 4:37: Because He loved your fathers, He chose their seed after them, even you, and Himself brought you forth out of Egypt by His great strength,
units.Deuteronomy 4:38: to destroy nations great and mightier than you from before you, to bring you in, and to give you their land to inherit, as you have this day.
units.Deuteronomy 4:39: And you shall know this day, and lay it to mind, that the Lord your God, He is God in heaven above and upon earth beneath; there is none beside Him.
units.Deuteronomy 4:40: And you shall keep His ordinances and His commandments which I command you this day, that it may be well with you and with your sons after you, and that you may prolong your days upon the land which the Lord your God gives you for ever.
units.Acts 2:14: Peter stood with the eleven, raised his voice, and addressed them: “Men of Judea and all who live in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and listen closely to my words.
units.Acts 2:15: These people are not drunk, as you suppose, for it is the third hour of the day.
units.Acts 2:16: Rather, this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:
units.Acts 2:17: ‘In the last days, God says, I will pour out of My Spirit upon all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy; your young men will see visions, and your elders will dream dreams.
units.Acts 2:18: Even upon My male slaves and My female slaves in those days I will pour out of My Spirit, and they will prophesy.
units.Acts 2:19: I will give wonders in heaven above and signs on the earth below: blood and fire and a cloud of smoke.
units.Acts 2:20: The sun will be changed into darkness and the moon into blood before the great and manifest day of the Lord comes.
units.Acts 2:21: And everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.’
units.Acts 2:22: Men of Israel, hear these words: Jesus the Nazarene was a man attested to you by God through mighty works, wonders, and signs that God did through Him in your midst, as you yourselves know.
units.Acts 2:23: This man, handed over according to God’s determined purpose and foreknowledge, you nailed up and killed through the hands of lawless men.
units.Acts 2:24: God raised Him, releasing Him from the pangs of death, because it was impossible for Him to be held by it.
units.Romans 10:9: Because if you confess Jesus as Lord with your mouth, and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved;
units.Romans 10:10: for with the heart one believes for righteousness, and with the mouth one confesses for salvation.
units.Romans 10:11: For the Scripture says, “Everyone who believes in Him will not be put to shame.”
units.Romans 10:12: For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek, for the same Lord is Lord of all, being rich toward all who call upon Him;
units.Romans 10:13: for “everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.”
units.Romans 10:14: How, then, are they to call upon One in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in One whom they have not heard? And how are they to hear without someone proclaiming?
units.Romans 10:15: And how are they to proclaim unless they are sent? Just as it is written, “How beautiful are the feet of those announcing good things!”
units.Ezekiel 36:1: “And you, son of man, prophesy concerning Israel’s mountains and say to Israel’s mountains, ‘Hear the Lord’s word:
units.Ezekiel 36:2: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Because the enemy said over you, “Well done! Everlasting wildernesses have become our possession,”
units.Ezekiel 36:3: therefore prophesy and say, Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Because you were dishonored and hated by those around you, so that you became a possession for the remaining nations, and you became a topic on people’s tongues and a reproach to nations,
units.Ezekiel 36:4: therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the Lord’s word! Thus says the Lord to the mountains, hills, ravines, torrents, devastated and destroyed places, and abandoned cities, which became plunder and a trampling place for the remaining nations all around:
units.Ezekiel 36:5: Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Surely in the fire of My wrath I have spoken against the remaining nations and all Idumea, because they gave My land to themselves as a possession with rejoicing, dishonoring lives so as to destroy through plunder.
units.Ezekiel 36:6: Therefore prophesy over Israel’s land and say to the mountains, hills, ravines and valleys, Thus says the Lord: Behold, I have spoken in My jealousy and My wrath because you bore the nations’ reproaches.
units.Ezekiel 36:7: Therefore I will raise My hand against the nations around you; these will receive their own dishonor.
units.Ezekiel 36:8: But your grapes and fruit, mountains of Israel, My people will consume, for they are drawing near.
units.2 Maccabees 8:1: Judas, also called Maccabeus, and those with him slipped secretly into the villages, called their kinsmen to join them, and gathered those who had remained in Judaism, assembling about six thousand.
units.2 Maccabees 8:2: They called upon the Lord to look upon the people trampled by everyone, and to have pity on the temple profaned by impious men,
units.2 Maccabees 8:3: to have mercy also on the city being destroyed and about to be levelled, and to listen to the blood crying out to Him,
units.2 Maccabees 8:4: to remember the unlawful destruction of innocent infants and the blasphemies committed against His name, and to show His hatred of wickedness.
units.2 Maccabees 8:5: Once Maccabeus had formed his company, he became irresistible to the nations, the Lord’s anger having turned to mercy.
units.2 Maccabees 8:6: Coming unexpectedly upon cities and villages, he burned them; seizing strategic places, he put not a few enemies to flight.
units.2 Maccabees 8:7: He especially used the nights as allies in such attacks. The report of his courage resounded everywhere.
units.2 Maccabees 8:8: Philip saw that the man was gradually advancing and making increasingly frequent progress in his successes. He wrote to Ptolemy, governor of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, to assist the king’s affairs.
units.2 Maccabees 8:9: Ptolemy quickly selected Nicanor son of Patroclus, one of the foremost friends, and sent him, placing under him no fewer than twenty thousand men from nations of every kind, to eradicate the whole people of Judea. He also associated with him Gorgias, a general experienced in military affairs.
units.2 Maccabees 8:10: Nicanor determined to discharge the king’s tribute to the Romans, amounting to two thousand talents, from the captivity of the Jews.
units.2 Maccabees 8:11: He immediately sent to the coastal cities, inviting people to buy Jewish bodies and promising to give ninety bodies for a talent, not expecting the judgment that was about to follow upon him from the Almighty.
units.2 Maccabees 8:12: News of Nicanor’s advance reached Judas. When he informed those with him of the army’s approach,
units.2 Maccabees 8:13: the cowardly and those who distrusted God’s judgment slipped away and left the place.
units.2 Maccabees 8:14: The others sold everything they had left and together begged the Lord to rescue those whom the impious Nicanor had sold before even encountering them,
units.2 Maccabees 8:15: if not for their own sake, then because of the covenants with their fathers and because His revered and magnificent name had been invoked over them.
units.Obadiah 1:1: The vision of Obadiah. Thus says the Lord God to Idumea: I heard a report from the Lord, and He sent a dispatch to the nations: “Rise up! Let us rise against her for battle!”
units.Obadiah 1:2: Look, I have made you insignificant among the nations; you are greatly dishonored.
units.Obadiah 1:3: The pride of your heart has lifted you up, you who camp in holes in the rocks, raising his dwelling high and saying in his heart, “Who will bring me down to the ground?”
units.Obadiah 1:4: If you soar like an eagle, and if you place your nest among the stars, from there I will bring you down, says the Lord.
units.Obadiah 1:5: If thieves came in to you, or robbers by night, where would you have been cast away? Would they not have stolen enough for themselves? And if grape gatherers came in to you, would they not have left a gleaning?
units.Obadiah 1:6: How Esau has been searched out, and his hidden things seized!
units.Obadiah 1:7: All the men of your covenant sent you out as far as your borders; the men at peace with you opposed you and prevailed over you. They set ambushes beneath you. There is no understanding in them.
units.Obadiah 1:8: On that day, says the Lord, I will destroy the wise from Idumea and understanding from Mount Esau.
units.Obadiah 1:9: Your warriors from Teman will be terrified, so that a person may be removed from Mount Esau,
units.Obadiah 1:10: because of the slaughter and the impiety toward your brother Jacob; and shame will cover you, and you will be removed forever.
units.Obadiah 1:11: From the day you stood opposed, on the day foreigners took his strength captive and strangers entered his gates and cast lots over Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.
units.Obadiah 1:12: Do not look on your brother’s day, on the day of strangers; do not rejoice over the sons of Judah on the day of their destruction; do not speak boastfully on the day of affliction.
units.Obadiah 1:13: Do not enter the gates of peoples on the day of their suffering. You, too, must not look on their assembly on the day of their destruction, and do not join in attacking their strength on the day of their destruction.
units.Obadiah 1:14: Do not stand at their escape routes to destroy those of them who are being saved, and do not shut in those fleeing from them on the day of affliction.
units.Obadiah 1:15: For the day of the Lord is near against all the nations. Just as you acted, so it will be for you; your recompense will be repaid upon your own head.
units.Obadiah 1:16: For just as you drank on My holy mountain, all the nations will drink wine; they will drink and go down, and they will be as though they did not exist.
units.Obadiah 1:17: But on Mount Zion there will be salvation, and it will be holy; the house of Jacob will possess those who possessed them.
units.Obadiah 1:18: The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble. They will blaze against them and consume them, and there will be no bearer of fire in the house of Esau, because the Lord has spoken.
units.Obadiah 1:19: Those in the Negeb will possess the mountain of Esau, and those in the Shephelah will possess the foreigners. They will possess the mountain of Ephraim, the plain of Samaria, Benjamin and the land of Gilead.
units.Obadiah 1:20: And this is the beginning of the deportation: for the sons of Israel, the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath; and the deportation of Jerusalem as far as Ephrathah. They will inherit the cities of the Negeb.
units.Obadiah 1:21: And men who have been saved shall ascend from Mount Zion to execute judgment upon the mountain of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s.
units.Daniel 1:1: In the third year of King Joakim of Judea, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon arrived at Jerusalem and besieged it.
units.Daniel 1:2: The Lord handed the city into his hands, together with Joakim king of Judea and a portion of the Lord’s sacred vessels. He carried them away to Babylon and deposited them in his idol-temple.
units.Daniel 1:3: The king told Abiesdri, his chief eunuch, to bring him some of the sons of Israel’s magnates, of the royal family and of the chosen men:
units.Daniel 1:4: young men without blemish, handsome, knowledgeable in every kind of wisdom, literate, intelligent, wise, and strong enough to be in the king’s house, and to teach them letters and the Chaldean tongue,
units.Amos 1:1: The words of Amos that came among nakkarim from Tekoa, which he saw concerning Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
units.Amos 1:2: He said: “The Lord spoke from Zion and gave His voice from Jerusalem; the shepherds’ pastures mourned, and Carmel’s summit dried up.”
units.Amos 1:3: The Lord said: “For three impieties of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they sawed the pregnant women of those in Gilead with iron saws.
units.Amos 1:4: I will send fire into Hazael’s house, and it will devour the foundations of the son of Ader,
units.Amos 1:5: and I will shatter Damascus’s bars and destroy inhabitants from the Plain of On. I will cut down a tribe from the men of Harran, and the people of Syria, called by name, will be taken captive,” says the Lord.

reread_versions.relationship: later express attribution of divine prophetic speech to Joel
reread_versions.rationale: The heading identifies the recipient of the Lord's word as Joel son of Bathuel. Peter introduces words spoken through the prophet Joel and quotes God's Spirit promise, matching Joel 3:1. That explicit quotation connects the book's named recipient with the later attribution; Acts does not repeat the father's name.
reread_versions.source_text: The word of the Lord that came to Joel, the son of Bathuel.

target_units.text: Rather, this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:
‘In the last days, God says, I will pour out of My Spirit upon all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy; your young men will see visions, and your elders will dream dreams.

reread_versions.relationship: parallel appeal to ancestral experience in describing extraordinary calamity
reread_versions.rationale: Joel asks whether the elders or their fathers have experienced such things. Exodus announces locusts filling Egyptian houses as neither fathers nor forefathers have seen. Both use ancestral experience to express the calamity's extraordinary character, without identifying the two events.
reread_versions.source_text: Hear these things, elders, and give ear, all who inhabit the land! Have such things happened in your days or in your fathers’ days?

target_units.text: And your houses shall be filled, and the houses of your attendants, and all the houses throughout the land of the Egyptians, as neither your fathers nor their forefathers have ever seen, from the day they came upon the earth to this day.” And Moses turned and went out from Pharaoh.

reread_versions.relationship: parallel commands to transmit the report through successive generations
reread_versions.rationale: Joel commands telling children, their children and a further generation. God tells Moses to recount His dealings with Egypt and His signs to children and grandchildren. The common instruction preserves the memory of the events across generations; Exodus explicitly names Egypt and God's signs.
reread_versions.source_text: Tell your children about these things, and let your children tell their children, and their children a further generation.

target_units.text: that you may tell in the ears of your children, and of your children’s children, how I have mocked the Egyptians, and My signs which I have performed among them; and you shall know that I am the Lord.”

reread_versions.relationship: parallel successive destruction of what an earlier calamity left
reread_versions.rationale: Joel describes each named devourer consuming what its predecessor left. Exodus describes locusts consuming what the hail left and the trees upon the land. The repeated destruction of the remainder connects the passages, while Joel's four named agents differ from the hail-and-locust sequence.
reread_versions.source_text: What the caterpillar left, the locust devoured; what the locust left, the bruchus locust devoured; what the bruchus locust left, the blight devoured.

target_units.text: And they shall cover the face of the land, and you shall not be able to see the land; and they shall devour all that remains of the land which the hail left to you, and every tree growing for you upon the land.

reread_versions.relationship: close calls to lament over wine and the loss of gladness
reread_versions.rationale: Joel summons drunkards and wine drinkers to weeping and lament because gladness and joy have been removed from their mouths. Isaiah commands wailing over wine and says the earth's gladness has ceased. The shared reversal is from wine-associated gladness to lament; Joel does not here say that wine itself has been removed.
reread_versions.source_text: Sober up, you drunkards, from their wine, and weep! Lament, all who drink wine to intoxication, because gladness and joy have been removed from your mouths.

target_units.text: Wail over wine everywhere! All the earth’s gladness has ceased.

reread_versions.relationship: parallel lion imagery for destructive invasion
reread_versions.rationale: Joel depicts the invading nation with a lion's teeth and a young lion's grinding teeth. Jeremiah describes a lion leaving its enclosure, destroying nations and making the land desolate. Both portray destructive invasion through lion imagery, with teeth specified in Joel and the lion's movement specified in Jeremiah.
reread_versions.source_text: For a nation has come up against My land, strong and uncountable. Its teeth are a lion’s teeth, and its grinding teeth a young lion’s.

target_units.text: A lion has gone up from his enclosure; destroying nations, he has set out and left his place to make the land a desolation, and cities will be demolished so that they are not inhabited.

reread_versions.relationship: parallel devastation of vines and fig cultivation by an invading nation
reread_versions.rationale: Joel's invading nation lays the vine waste and shatters the fig trees. Jeremiah's distant nation devours vineyards, fig orchards and olive groves along with other produce. Both name vines and figs among the invasion's agricultural losses; Joel additionally describes whitened branches.
reread_versions.source_text: It laid My vine waste and shattered My fig trees; searching, it searched it out and cast it away; it whitened its branches.

target_units.text: and they will devour your harvest and your bread, and devour your sons and daughters, and devour your sheep and calves, and devour your vineyards and fig orchards and olive groves; and with a sword they will thresh your fortified cities, in which you have trusted.

reread_versions.relationship: parallel sackcloth lament expressed through grief for a beloved person
reread_versions.rationale: Joel commands lament greater than that of a bride in sackcloth for her first husband. Jeremiah tells the daughter of his people to put on sackcloth and make mourning for a beloved one. The commands combine sackcloth with bereavement imagery; the bride and first husband are particular to Joel.
reread_versions.source_text: Lament to Me more than a bride wrapped in sackcloth for her first husband.

target_units.text: Daughter of My people, gird yourself with sackcloth; sprinkle yourself with ashes. Make mourning for yourself for a beloved one, a pitiful lament, because misery will suddenly come upon you.

reread_versions.relationship: related loss of fitting offerings and drink at the Lord's house
reread_versions.rationale: Joel says sacrifice and drink offering have been removed from the Lord's house. Hosea says they did not pour wine to the Lord, describes defiling sacrifices, and says their loaves will not enter His house. The connection concerns disrupted food-and-drink worship, while removal and defilement remain different descriptions.
reread_versions.source_text: Sacrifice and drink offering have been removed from the Lord’s house. Mourn, priests who minister at the altar,

target_units.text: They did not pour wine to the Lord or make it pleasant to Him. Their sacrifices are like bread of mourning to them; all who eat them will be defiled, because their loaves for their own lives will not enter the Lord’s house.

reread_versions.relationship: parallel judgment affecting grain, wine and oil
reread_versions.rationale: Joel describes suffering grain, dried wine and diminished oil. Haggai announces withheld dew and produce, followed by a sword upon the land, grain, wine and oil. The same three agricultural staples appear within judgment on the land; Haggai's explicit sword is not replaced with a drought statement.
reread_versions.source_text: because the plains have suffered. Let the earth mourn, because grain has suffered, wine has dried up, and oil has diminished.

target_units.text: therefore heaven will hold back dew, and the earth will withhold its produce.
I will bring a sword upon the land and the mountains, upon grain, wine and oil, and whatever the earth produces, upon people and livestock, and upon all the labors of their hands.”

reread_versions.relationship: related distress of cultivators when the land's produce fails
reread_versions.rationale: Joel says the farmers have dried up and commands the estates to lament the lost wheat and barley harvest. Jeremiah says the land's works failed for lack of rain and the farmers were ashamed and covered their heads. Agricultural failure affects the cultivators in both, while their stated conditions differ.
reread_versions.source_text: The farmers have dried up. Lament, estates, over wheat and barley, because the harvest from the field has perished.

target_units.text: And the land’s works failed because there was no rain; the farmers were ashamed and covered their heads.

reread_versions.relationship: paired failure and renewed fruitfulness of vine and fig tree
reread_versions.rationale: The vine dries up and fig trees diminish in the lament. The later reassurance says the tree bore fruit and vine and fig tree gave their strength. These named plants connect the desolation with the promised renewal, without replacing this source's separate statement that people put joy to shame.
reread_versions.source_text: The vine has dried up and the fig trees have diminished; pomegranate, palm, apple tree and all the field’s trees have dried up, because human beings have put joy to shame.

target_units.text: Take courage, animals of the plain, because the wilderness plains have sprouted, because a tree bore its fruit; vine and fig tree have given their strength.

reread_versions.relationship: same-chapter expansion of the priests' mourning over removed offerings
reread_versions.rationale: Both units address ministers at the altar and connect their mourning with sacrifice and drink offering kept from God's house. This later summons adds wrapping themselves, beating their breasts and sleeping in sackcloth to the earlier instruction to mourn.
reread_versions.source_text: Wrap yourselves and beat your breasts, priests; lament, ministers of the altar! Enter and sleep in sackcloth, ministers of God, because sacrifice and drink offering have been kept away from your God’s house.

target_units.text: Sacrifice and drink offering have been removed from the Lord’s house. Mourn, priests who minister at the altar,

reread_versions.relationship: repeated summons to a consecrated fast and gathered congregation
reread_versions.rationale: The earlier call consecrates a fast, proclaims a service and gathers elders and the land's inhabitants. The later call repeats the fast and service, then explicitly includes nursing infants, bridegroom and bride in the gathering. The repeated commands connect the communal responses while preserving the added participants.
reread_versions.source_text: Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service. Gather elders, all who inhabit the land, into your God’s house, and cry earnestly to the Lord,

target_units.text: Blow a trumpet in Zion! Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service.
Gather the people; consecrate the congregation. Choose elders; gather infants nursing at breasts. Let the bridegroom leave his bedroom and the bride her bridal chamber.

reread_versions.relationship: close announcement of the Lord's near day with lament and suffering
reread_versions.rationale: Joel laments the near day of the Lord and says it comes like suffering from suffering. Isaiah likewise commands wailing because the Lord's day is near and shattering will come from God. The shared warning does not replace Joel's stated comparison with Isaiah's explicit naming of God as the source of shattering.
reread_versions.source_text: “Alas, alas, alas for the day! For the Lord’s day is near, and it will come like suffering from suffering.”

target_units.text: Wail, for the Lord’s day is near, and shattering will come from God.

reread_versions.relationship: contrast between lost food and sanctuary joy and commanded festal eating
reread_versions.rationale: Joel reports food destroyed before the people's eyes and gladness and joy lost from God's house. Deuteronomy directs the people to bring offerings to the chosen place, eat before the Lord and rejoice. The loss reverses the conjunction of nourishment and glad worship described in the command.
reread_versions.source_text: Before your eyes food was destroyed, and gladness and joy from your God’s house.

target_units.text: but unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose in one of your tribes, to set His name there, that it may be called upon, you shall seek and come thither.
